doc.title: Ray Shiner interviewed by Monk Rowe, Clinton, New York, October 11, 1998

title: Practical jokes in the band
summary: Band full of jokers; balloons popped during his tenor solo on Manhattan.

story.theme_name: Band pranks, jokes and gigs gone wrong
story.community_name: Pranks, practical jokes and band humor

blocks.x: Did you guys have practical jokers in the band?
Oh yeah. We had 21 musicians on the band, and 21 practical jokers. Nineteen musicians and two leaders.
What was the worst thing that you ever pulled, can you recall?
Oh it’s hard to describe. I can’t describe that one.
Well how about the second worst?

Well the second worst was I stood up to play a tenor sax solo on “Manhattan,” it was written for me, a special arrangement, I had dear friends in the audience waiting to hear every note, and it was at a public dance, and they had balloons there, and as soon as I stood up to play the tenor sax solo, somebody started putting pins, popping balloons, which killed it.
